source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 3 and 5; Appendix D, “Understanding prediction intervals for individual treatment effect when the outcome is ordinal”
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited version studies ITE prediction intervals, extends discussion to ordinal outcomes, and labels its sharp ordinal pmf result Theorem 12; the supplied “following Theorem 16” anchor is not present in this version.
The paper investigates the finite Strassen/Hall equivalence and presents a combinatorial route to a finite Strassen theorem.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics 43(5), 2018
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives sharp bounds for the probabilities that treatment is beneficial and strictly beneficial under fixed potential-outcome marginals.
The paper constructs minimum-average-volume confidence regions for a multinomial/categorical probability vector and discusses linear-functional intervals.
The paper constructs a pointwise-consistent confidence interval for the partially identified fraction who benefit with ordinal or binary outcomes using stochastic optimization.
The paper gives a distribution-free dynamic-programming method with near-optimal volume among unions of k intervals under ordinary conformal prediction coverage.
The paper concerns sharp bounds on the distribution of treatment effects and their statistical inference, making it an essential adjacent comparator for the interval-price theorem.
